To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

EAA + carbohydrate (CHO) ingestion before a bout resistance exercise prevents the exercise-induced decrease of muscle protein synthesis and results in an enhanced rate postexercise muscle protein during postexercise recovery.
EAA + carbohydrate ingestion before resistance training exercise does not enhance muscle protein synthesis compared with exercise alone.
EAA + carbohydrate ingestion before a bout resistance exercise does not improve the rate of muscle protein synthesis during the postexercise recovery period.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of muscle protein synthesis during and following resistance exercise.
the effect of EAA + carbohydrate ingestion before a bout high-intensity resistance exercise on muscle protein synthesis during exercise and recovery.

the effects of EAA + carbohydrate (CHO) ingestion before and following a bout of resistance-type exercise on postexercise skeletal muscle fractional synthetic rate (FSR) and cell signaling proteins associated to the regulation of muscle protein synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ingestion of EAA + 7.5% glucose solution before a bout of high intensity resistance exercise prevents the exercise-induced decline in muscle FSR, but the ingestion of this solution before exercise does not enhance the rate of muscle FSA during recovery.
ingestion of EAA + 7% glucose (EAA + 0.7 g CHO/kg) before resistance exercise does increase muscle FSR during the preexercise period and does not enhance post-exercise muscle protein synthesis.
EAA + CH ingestion before exercise does not improve postexercise muscle protein anabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EAA + CH ingestion before exercise is not necessary and that the timing of EAA + CH intake should occur after exercise to enhance postexercise FRS.
EAA + CH ingestion before resistance exercise may be beneficial for the athlete, but not for the general population.
EAA + carbohydrate ingestion before exercise is not an effective nutritional strategy to enhance muscle FSR during recovery from resistance exercise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EAA + carbohydrate ingestion before exercise does not improve the postexercise muscle protein synthetic response to resistance exercise in young, healthy subjects.
EAA + carbohydrate ingestion before resistance does not improve muscle protein synthesis during the postexercise recovery period.
EAA + protein ingestion before resistance exercise is not necessary for the stimulation of postexercise protein synthesis.
